events.text: A tea-steward on the Sixth Isle bars the steeping-house door while you are still inside. {He} sets out two bowls of cloud-tea and lets the steam climb a full breath before speaking. "You came up the stairs angry," {he} says. "Anger keeps well up here. But there is a place to put it."

choices.text: Stay and learn the steeping

effects.log: {npc} corrects your wrist nine times. By the tenth bowl you have forgotten the quarrel you carried up the stairs. (Cloud-Steeping Way begun.)

choices.text: Thank {him} for the bowl and go

effects.log: Fine leaf. {npc} nods as if that were also an answer.

events.text: A ledger-keeper of the Jade Court watches you count stones outside a lane exchange and clucks. "Three errors, all in the house's favour." {He} draws a counting-rod set from {his} sleeve as another immortal might draw a sword. "Sit. Interest is the only thing up here that climbs without a stair."

choices.text: Learn the keeper's method

effects.log: By dusk you have found the three errors and two more nobody mentioned. (Ledger-Reckoning of the Isles begun.)

choices.text: Say stones are not your road

effects.log: "They are everyone's road," {npc} says, and goes back to the exchange to wait for the next one.

events.text: A cloud-herder with a horn-scarred ear is combing frost from a sky-elk at an isle's edge, and tells you without turning that a wind-serpent trailed you across two bridges. "It let you walk. Do you know why?" {He} points the comb at the cloud-dust behind your heels, where you finally see the track.

choices.text: Sit and learn to read it

effects.log: {npc} walks you through a winter of spoor in one afternoon, and gives you a vial for your trouble. (Sky-Beast Lore begun.)

choices.text: Thank {him} and cross by the other bridge

effects.log: You cross by the other bridge. You sleep well.

events.text: A terrace-keeper on a drifting orchard-isle takes a stalk out of your hand before you finish plucking it. "That one sours the whole row for a decade," {he} says, and reads the terraces once, the way a registrar reads a petition. "What you want grows leeward. Nobody told you. Come."

choices.text: Follow {him} along the terraces

effects.log: You come down with a basket, and a slope you will never see the same way again. (Orchard-Reading begun.)

choices.text: Keep your own basket

effects.log: You pick where you were picking. You leave out the one that sours rows.

events.text: A hermit has sat at a bridge-shrine over the Sea of Clouds since before your last ascent, and lichen has crept up {his} sleeve. When you pass back at dusk {his} eyes open. "Your breath leaks," {he} says, like noting a roof. "Each failed climb you spill a decade. Why do you do that?"

choices.text: Ask {him} how not to

effects.log: One breath a day for a month, then fewer. You had not known how much of you was hurrying. (Tortoise-Isle Breath begun.)

choices.text: Leave a spirit stone in the bowl and go on

effects.log: The eyes close again. The lichen has not noticed you were there.

events.text: A ferryman lies pinned under a fallen cloud-skiff, and an ancient healer-immortal kneels beside the wreck and looks up. "You. Broad shoulders. Hold the knee, and watch what my hands do, because I am very old and not one house on these isles has ever watched."

choices.text: Hold the knee, and watch

effects.log: There is one soft sound, and the groaning stops. {npc} shows you the trick again on a fish-bone over supper. (Jade-Bone Setting begun.)

choices.text: Hold the knee, and leave when it is done

effects.log: It is done quickly. You do not ask how, and you are not sure you wanted to know.

events.text: A lantern-isle troupe lashes a silk cord at a moth on your hat brim: the moth is gone, the hat is not. Their lead lifts a coin off a child's ear the same way and gives it back. "Soft things go around," {he} tells you. "Everyone here wants the crack. You watched the wrist."

choices.text: Ask about the wrist

effects.log: Three weeks with the troupe and a welt on every part of you, and one dawn the cord does what you meant. (Cloud-Silk Lash begun.)

choices.text: Applaud and move on

effects.log: A coin tossed by the man beside you never lands. It reaches {his} hand, by the cord.

events.text: A disgraced examiner of the Jade Court duels a drunk immortal outside a wine-barge, using a sword like a corrector's brush. Three strokes, and the drunk's sash reads "fool" in running script. {npc} sees you staring. "You write as well," {he} says. "Most who do both are ashamed of one."

choices.text: Say you are ashamed of neither

effects.log: {npc} laughs until {he} coughs, then writes you a page of strokes with a blade, on a door. It takes you a year to read. (Ink-Cloud Sword begun.)

choices.text: Fetch {him} the next jar instead

effects.log: A good evening. By its end {he} has insulted everyone you know, accurately.

events.text: A blind storyteller in a lantern-house stops mid-verse to announce that a courier two isles over has just dropped a tray of cups. The room laughs. Ten breaths later, far below, something shatters on a landing. Afterwards {he} finds you. "You turned your head. Shall I show you how the wind is read?"

choices.text: Yes, and sit with your eyes shut

effects.log: A season in a dark room beside a stranger's breathing. Then one night you know who is climbing the stair. (Wind-Ear Art begun.)

choices.text: Ask only what the courier carried

effects.log: "A seal for the Ledger," says {npc}. You move to a different inn.

events.text: You buy a candied plum from an old woman on the dock on Monday. On Tuesday a young guard asks how the plum was, in the same voice. {npc} laughs at your face. "Nobody looks at a face up here. They look at your aura, and an aura is only a posture. I have watched you. You could wear many."

choices.text: Learn the borrowed posture

effects.log: For a month you are a porter, then a pilgrim, then nobody. Your oldest friend would pass you on a bridge. (Thousand Masks of the Mist begun.)

choices.text: Decline, and watch your sleeve

effects.log: Your sleeve is as you left it. A plum stone has been slipped inside.

events.text: An old standard-bearer of the Isle-Host, which lost its last war on a bridge of cloud, keeps the banners in a lacquer box and lays them out among the tea-bowls. "This is the bridge," {he} says. "You hold a hundred immortals, and fog. Tell me what you do, and I will tell you when they fall."

choices.text: Move a tea-bowl

effects.log: Your hundred are lost six times before the tea is cold. On the seventh {npc} studies the table without speaking. (Banner of the Isle-Host begun.)

choices.text: Say the war is long over

effects.log: "It is," {npc} says, and puts away the banners one at a time, in the order they fell.

events.text: At a soul-lantern floating over a drowned isle, one mourner hums beneath the others' chant, a line that makes your teeth feel far away. {He} stops when {he} sees you listening. "Your ear is not for the living," {he} says, not unkindly. "Most would have felt nothing."

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you the line

effects.log: It has no words. It has an order in which you stop being afraid of things. You learn the first of them that winter. (Soul-Bell Chant begun.)

choices.text: Pay your respects and leave

effects.log: You set a stone on the lantern rim. The line follows you across one bridge and then lets you go.

events.text: A recluse on a bare tooth of rock watches you run your breath, and winces as if bitten. "That method and your root are quarrelling. You will win, and it will take your age. Wood feeds fire. Do you know what that means, or do you only recall the line?"

choices.text: Admit you only recall the line

effects.log: You breathe in a circle for a hundred days, wood to fire to earth, until your root stops arguing. (Five-Element Turning begun.)

choices.text: Say your method has served you well

effects.log: "It has," says {npc}. "Ask it what it charged."

events.text: On a schooling-isle the dullest pupil in three generations has been given one sum since plum-blossom. You watch the instructor try a ninth way, and a tenth. On the eleventh the child looks up. {npc} sees you see it. "Anyone can do it once," {he} says. "Do you want to learn to do it again?"

choices.text: Take the bench beside {him} for a season

effects.log: You are very bad at it. Then one afternoon somebody's child understands, and you have to step outside. (Lamp-Handing Art begun.)

choices.text: Leave a gift for the schooling-isle

effects.log: The child carries it to the instructor with both hands, and has counted it correctly.

events.text: On the White Stairs a tiny old porter overtakes you with a brazier on {his} back, descends, and overtakes you again. "You stop to breathe," {he} says on the third pass. "That is why you must stop. Will you carry something?"

choices.text: Take a brazier

effects.log: You carry braziers for a month and learn to climb the way water comes down. (White-Stair Breath begun.)

choices.text: Sit on the step and tell {him} to go on

effects.log: You sit. The view of the Sea is very fine. {npc} passes twice more before you rise.

events.text: A rival from the house across the lane has come to your tea-room to kill you, and is drinking your cloud-tea. You both know. You pour again, slowly, and watch the tremor leave {his} hand before it leaves yours. Meditation now begins at the fifth breath. You wonder if {he} can tell.

choices.text: Ask {him} who sent {him}, between bowls

effects.log: {npc} tells you on the third bowl and asks for a fourth. By morning the lane has one fewer feud, and nobody is hurt.

choices.text: Say nothing, and see {him} to the bridge

effects.log: The tale crosses three isles. People begin to arrive at your door who do not drink.

events.text: A skiff-hound breaks loose on the Fourth Isle dock with a child on its tow-line. Your cord is round its collar before you decide anything, and then you are holding a beast. Afterwards {npc}, a beast-broker, wipes {his} hands. "You never hurt its mouth. I have one nobody can touch. It wants a hand like that."

choices.text: Go and look at the beast

effects.log: It bites you, then stops. You leave with a vial of its essence, freely given, and an offer of work. What you best on the road may now follow you home.

choices.text: Return the child and go

effects.log: The mother cannot speak. The hound tries to follow you for a while.

events.text: Your own form has not moved for a decade, and you copy an old poem to rest. Halfway down the slip you notice that the third stroke is the form. You stop and look at your hand. A bill-collector of the Jade Court stands in the door and has seen your face. "Shall I come back?" {he} says.

choices.text: Ask {him} to come back

effects.log: You write until the lamp dies. Your own art comes easier now, as anything does that has been written once.

choices.text: Settle the bill, then return to the slip

effects.log: It does not go away. It waits, as a good line does.

events.text: You share a ferry with two hunters of the Celestial Ministries who carry your likeness on a slip. One reads it aloud. "Tall, left-handed, walks as if owed." You are a stout fog-fish seller with a cough, asking {npc} about the price of eels. Their eyes slide over you like water.

choices.text: Offer them a fish

effects.log: One of them buys a fish from you. It is the most frightening thing you have done this age. They go on searching, farther away.

choices.text: Step off at the next landing

effects.log: You step off. A century later you hear they are still riding that route.

events.text: At a muster of an Eight House's isle-guard you are asked, as a courtesy, to look over the line. You move four spears and a standard. {npc}, their captain, stares at the field a long while and sends for an old map. "A house could be beaten from here," {he} says. "If anyone ever wished it."

choices.text: Draw {him} the map

effects.log: Your name begins to turn up where a fighter's name does not. In any war your faction joins, people will stand where you tell them.

choices.text: Tell {him} to burn the map

effects.log: {npc} burns it. You watch the smoke, then draw it again, for yourself, from memory.

events.text: You are humming in a sickroom for nobody in particular, and the dying elder sits up to say that {npc} is at the door. {npc} is. "It is your humming," the elder says. "It goes further than you do." You feel it then, the part of you that lives past the isle's edge.

choices.text: Keep humming, and follow it

effects.log: You sit up with it until dawn. Your soul sits a little farther out in you than it did yesterday.

choices.text: Stop, and see who is at the door

effects.log: {npc} has brought soup. You are grateful for a door with only somebody at it.

events.text: A pupil you gave up on returns after a century with a House seal at the belt. {npc} bows to you on the stair before everyone, then repeats something you once said that you do not recall saying. {He} has built a whole ascent on it.

choices.text: Pretend you remember

effects.log: You nod slowly, and {npc} is delighted. You spend the evening afraid of the things you might have said.

choices.text: Admit you do not remember

effects.log: {npc} laughs for a long time. "That is the best thing you ever taught me." You will be asked to teach again.

events.text: A partner at your lane-house brings the year's tallies with a pleasant smile. You read them as you would a stance, and on the eleventh slip find the one figure standing badly. {npc} watches your finger stop. {He} has stopped smiling, and is working out what you know.

choices.text: Say nothing, and have the figure corrected

effects.log: The missing stones turn up next month with a note about a clerk. Your tallies have not been wrong since.

choices.text: Ask {him} about it before the staff

effects.log: {npc} leaves the lane. Every clerk you keep now sits a little straighter.

events.text: On a landing of the White Stairs where you once sat a whole season gasping, you find you have come up still breathing as on level ground. {npc}, a climber slumped against the rail with a sword across the knees, looks up. "Are you even tired?"

choices.text: Sit and show {him} the breath

effects.log: You sit with {npc} for an hour. The Stairs do not seem to mind. Neither of you is anyone in particular, for that hour.

choices.text: Say "Not yet," and go on up

effects.log: You go on. Your breath is the only sound on the stair, and it does not change.

events.text: You taste the ash for days. Then a stranger stops you on a cloud-bridge, calls you by a name you never had, and asks if you have finally paid. {He} does not seem surprised at your silence. "It is a start," says {npc}, and walks on. You have three years less and feel lighter.

choices.text: Go after {him} and ask the name

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It means nothing. In the night you remember what it means.

choices.text: Let {him} go, and leave stones at the next shrine

effects.log: You leave two stones at the next shrine, and two at the one after. It becomes a habit you did not ask for.

choices.text: Let {him} go

effects.log: You watch {him} cross. The lightness stays a little longer than you expected.

events.text: You are at a tea-barge far below the isles, among people who should not know you, when someone in the next compartment tells {npc} how you died. The telling is good. The teller was in the cell. You hear the cold of you, and the cart, and sit with your noodles through the part where the warden wept.

choices.text: Stay dead for a while

effects.log: It is restful. Nobody asks anything of the dead.

choices.text: Send the teller a jug

effects.log: The teller stares at you a long time and accepts it. The story is better the next night.

events.text: The sickness of the Hollow Cup lasts a month. When you can stand, you test yourself with a lesser pill, and it takes as it did in your youth. {npc}, a pill-steward, studies your tongue and your eyes. "You will not find that twice," {he} says. "Spend it on something."

choices.text: Ask what {he} would spend it on

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It is not what you expected, and it is not a pill.

choices.text: Buy the best {he} has

effects.log: It is good, and you feel it land.

choices.text: Thank {him} and rest another week

effects.log: The week passes in a quiet room. You are strangely content.

events.text: The Root-Shifting Pearl has done its work, and your old method runs without its old quarrel. Then an elder of your root's own element meets you on a landing and stops dead. "What have you done?" says {npc}, staring at something you cannot see. "It leans. Your root leans. Who did that to you?"

choices.text: Say you did it yourself

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as at an interesting ruin. {He} writes it down.

choices.text: Ask whether it can be read

effects.log: {npc} reads it, on the landing, two fingers at your wrist. {He} never stops frowning, and never stops reading.

events.text: Evening in a lowland village the cloud-roads never touch. The neighbours have brought out the thin wine, and {npc} is telling the one about the goat for the fifth time this season. You laugh in the right place. You did not have to remember to. Far below you, something sealed turns over in its sleep.

choices.text: Tell the goat story yourself next time

effects.log: You tell it badly. It becomes your story anyway. They begin to call it yours.

choices.text: Go home early and sit with it

effects.log: You sit. It is quiet. You are, you notice, not unhappy, and you leave that alone.

events.text: A tutor comes to your door with a slate. {He} has taught the young one of your house for a season and has now been corrected, on a point held for thirty years, by a child eating a plum. "I do not know what you did," says {npc}. "I would like to know what you intend to do about it."

choices.text: Send for finer teachers, at any price

effects.log: They come, and one by one they leave, somewhat quieter. The child does not notice them go.

choices.text: Ask {him} to stay and be corrected

effects.log: {npc} stays, and it is the happiest {he} has been in years. The two argue at breakfast.

events.text: Your neighbour {npc} stops you on the cloud-path and asks what you did. The old one in your house was up on the roof this morning, mending it, shouting down about a debt from twenty years ago. "We were all so sure," {he} says. {He} does not sound entirely pleased. "Is there any more of it?"

choices.text: Send over a bowl of plain soup

effects.log: It is only soup. {npc} is better within the week, and tells everyone.

choices.text: Say it will not work on those who ask

effects.log: {npc} laughs and almost believes you. You go up and help with the roof.

events.text: They say you can see it on those who tried an ascent on a Sunfire pill. {npc}, an old gate-warden of some forgotten house, sees it on you across a landing. {He} points to {his} own throat, where the scar runs down. "Once," {he} says. "We all think once. Did it open?"

choices.text: Say what happened

effects.log: {npc} hears all of it, then tells you {his} own, which is much worse, and asks you to stop there.

choices.text: Ask who sells them

effects.log: {npc} tells you, and looks away first.
